comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological claims (C9-C10, C31-C41). Both evaluations accept the basic experimental procedures, sample sizes, behavioral performance metrics, and data collection methods. OpenEval notes the small sample size limitation while peer reviewers focus concerns on analysis rather than methodology.

Major disagreement on remapping patterns (C12-C17). OpenEval finds the ANCOVA controls adequate and the remapping patterns well-supported. Peer reviewers express major concern that behavioral confounds (location, speed, head direction) are not properly controlled, particularly on the maze stem, and fear the ANCOVAs fail to detect these confounds, undermining the conclusions.

Complete agreement on background/literature claims (C1-C2, C5-C8, C11, C22-C25, C34). Both evaluations accept these established knowledge claims from prior research as appropriately cited context. Neither evaluation challenges the characterization of existing literature.

Disagreement on classifier results and episodic processing (C19-C21). OpenEval finds the journey prediction and trial type classification well-supported by rigorous methods, though notes C21 extends beyond direct observation. Peer reviewers request additional analysis on relative classification ability across trajectories, tasks, and trial types, indicating insufficient evidence for the episodic integration claim.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding hierarchical organization (C27-C28 overlap). Both evaluations find this theoretical conclusion insufficiently supported. OpenEval notes heavy reliance on inference and need for additional experiments. Peer reviewers find the hierarchical organization concept difficult to follow and Figure 7 hard to interpret, requesting better analysis and presentation.

Agreement on uncertainty for primary conclusions (C3, C26 overlap with C3, C18, C26-C28). Both evaluations question whether the data adequately support the interpretive framework. OpenEval notes conflation of observation with interpretation and lack of causal mechanisms. Peer reviewers find the hierarchical organization presentation inadequate and difficult to follow.

Agreement on uncertainty for dual role claim (C4). Both evaluations question this overarching conclusion. OpenEval finds it an interpretive framework not directly tested. Peer reviewers' uncertainty stems from concerns about underlying remapping data quality and unclear hierarchical framework presentation.

Agreement on uncertainty for functional claims (C30). Both evaluations find the spatial navigation and episodic memory claims speculative. OpenEval characterizes them as extrapolations rather than directly tested hypotheses. Peer reviewers' uncertainty derives from concerns about both data quality and interpretive framework clarity.

Partial overlap on classifier results (C18). OpenEval supports the journey prediction findings with rigorous cross-validation methods. Peer reviewers group C18 with hierarchical organization claims (C3, C26-C28) and find the overall presentation difficult to follow, creating uncertainty about the generalization interpretation.
